items.title: Associated factors for stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis or septic shock: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Stress ulcers and gut bleeding in sepsis are linked to patient, illness and treatment factors, not one single cause.
ai.summary: A systematic review of six observational studies involving 131,568 adults with sepsis or septic shock found that stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding affected between 2.0% and 32.3% of patients. Associated factors included older age, previous gut bleeding, liver disease, cancer, kidney problems, shock, mechanical ventilation and certain medicines.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows doctors may need to decide who gets ulcer-preventing treatment based on individual risk rather than giving it to everyone with sepsis.
ai.fact: Stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in sepsis are linked to factors such as shock, kidney problems, liver disease, previous gut bleeding and mechanical ventilation.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the rate of stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding in people with sepsis or septic shock?
quiz.answer: Across six studies, the rate varied between 2.0% and 32.3%.

ai.caveat: The review combined observational studies, which can show links but cannot prove that these factors cause stress ulcers or bleeding.

ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at studies from Western Asia, South Asia and Africa on mental health and thinking problems after traumatic brain injury. It found depression in about 35%, anxiety in about 29%, PTSD in about 20%, OCD in about 19%, sleep disturbance in about 27% and cognitive impairment in about 49% of people studied.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that brain injury can be followed by common mental health and thinking difficulties, so people recovering from head injuries may benefit from checking for these issues.
ai.life_skill: Notice changes in mood, sleep or thinking after a head injury and mention them to a healthcare professional.
ai.fact: Cognitive impairment was the most frequently reported problem after traumatic brain injury in the regions studied.

quiz.question: Which problem was most common after traumatic brain injury in this review?
quiz.answer: Cognitive impairment, found in about 49% of people studied.

ai.caveat: The studies used different diagnostic tools and measures, so the results are not perfectly consistent.
